banner.title: SUGCON
banner.metaDescription: Relationship building at SUGCON India — connections with organizers, Sitecore community voices, and conversation starters that stick.
banner.headline: SUGCON is where relationships compound.
banner.intro: The sessions matter. The hallway conversations matter more. These are the people I met, the moments we shared, and the talking points that keep the Sitecore community moving forward — from SUGCON India 2024 through 2026.

sections.peopleLede: Names, faces, and the notes I want to remember — not a speaker list, a connection list.
sections.insightsTitle: Points worth carrying into the next chat
sections.insightsLede: Session highlights that became follow-up topics with the people above — framing, not a transcript.
sections.momentsLede: Proof of presence — booths, backdrops, and the people standing beside you.

connections.name: Sebastian Winter
connections.connectionNote: Met Sebastian across two SUGCON India editions — as organizer and community anchor. These photos are reminders that showing up year after year turns a handshake into a real working relationship in the Sitecore ecosystem.

connections.name: Rob
connections.connectionNote: Connected at the Altudo booth and around the venue — the kind of easy, generous conversation that makes SUGCON feel like a reunion, not a trade show. Booth chats, lobby catch-ups, and team photos that capture the real reason we travel for these events.

connections.name: Sailash Tirkey and Sumit Kumar
connections.connectionNote: Shared the floor with Sailash, Sumit and the Altudo crew — celebrating organizers, sponsors, and the people who make SUGCON feel like home. Team presence turns individual networking into lasting community goodwill.

insights.title: Be headless-curious
insights.summary: Stay · Blend · Modern — you do not have to rewrite your site.
insights.detail: Three paths on one content tree: stay on Sitecore MVC, blend hybrid MVC + headless components, or go full headless with JSS / .NET Rendering SDK when the brief calls for it. A practical framing I keep sharing in follow-up chats after SUGCON.

insights.title: Stay current — prefer 10.5
insights.summary: Get to 10.4 or 10.5 for the longest runway into vNext.
insights.detail: Modern third-party stack, .NET 10 where it applies, and upgrade muscle as a habit — not a leap. This slide became one of my favorite conversation openers with peers planning their next release train.

insights.title: Orchestrate agentic workflows
insights.summary: Agent API and Marketer MCP in your environment of choice.
insights.detail: Keynote energy around building agentic workflows where marketers and developers already work. A natural bridge from platform talk to how teams actually collaborate — which is what SUGCON relationships are for.
